tables.heading_context: ## Trophic Cascades — The Same Story Four Times
rows: Yellowstone: wolf removal → elk overgrazing → riparian collapse → stream erosion → fewer beaver → simplified hydrology
Carpenter experiments: bass removal → minnow explosion → zooplankton crash → algal bloom → turbid, anoxic lake
Suppress predatory arthropods → bacterial grazers explode → N mineralization rate spikes → nutrient pulse → plant community shift
Overfishing sharks → mesopredator release → herbivore decline → algae overgrow coral → reef flattens → biodiversity collapses

tables.heading_context: ## The Ecologist's Diagnostic — Five Questions at Every Scale
rows: Allochthonous (leaf litter) in headwaters; autochthonous (algae) in mid-reaches
Detritus from above; root exudates below
Mycorrhizal fungi + decomposers in litter layer
Bacterial biofilms on substrate; macroinvertebrate shredders
Tight coral-zooxanthellae N/P recycling loop; sponge loop
Mast-producing oaks (Fagaceae) -- acorn crop drives mammal/bird populations
Top predatory fish -- regulate everything below via trophic cascade
Mycorrhizal fungi -- 80-90% of plant species depend on them for P uptake
Herbivorous fish and urchins -- keep algae off coral, maintaining the reef's light budget
Fire, windthrow, insect outbreak → gap dynamics → successional mosaic
Flood pulse → lateral connectivity → floodplain renewal
Tillage, erosion, compaction → horizon disruption → century-scale recovery
Cyclones, bleaching events → partial mortality → 10-30 year recovery if stress is removed
Even-aged monoculture; no understory; no mast → faunal crash
Eutrophic, turbid, anoxic; invasive-dominated; no EPT invertebrates
Compacted, salinized, SOM < 1%; biological desert; erosion > formation
Phase shift: algae-dominated, structurally flat, no fish recruitment, net CaCO₃ dissolution
Bare ground → lichen → grass → shrub → pioneer → canopy
Bare channel → biofilm → algae → invertebrates → fish → riffle-pool
Fresh rock → weathering → lichen → A horizon → full profile
Bare substrate → coralline algae → recruits → massive colonies → framework
Canopy intercepts 80-95% of light; boreal decomposition is slow, so N recycles sluggishly
N-fixation by cyanobacteria can compensate for N scarcity; P has no atmospheric source
Phosphorus (old weathered soils), nitrogen (young soils), water (arid)
P binds irreversibly to Fe/Al oxides in old soils; N volatilizes or leaches
Zooxanthellae need light; CaCO₃ precipitation requires supersaturated seawater
